verdict_reasoning: No objection survived the critic. The only one raised, maintenance-fit-1, was refuted because each GiST opclass already keeps its own picksplit. The patch fixes a measured defect in an existing contrib opclass, copies the box and point approach, and adds no user-visible surface. Confidence is medium because nobody has reviewed v2 and no numbers exist for v2.

brief.title: Double-sorting page split for contrib/cube GiST
brief.problem: The cube GiST opclass uses Guttman's polynomial split, which can put almost all entries on one side of a split. With sorted input, insertion becomes quadratic and the index grows very large. This affects users of contrib/cube with GiST indexes.
brief.proposed_design: The patch replaces the cube picksplit with the double-sorting split used by the built-in box and point GiST opclasses, generalized to any number of dimensions. Absent dimensions count as zero, the same minimum split ratio applies, and an even split is the fallback. v2 uses float8 ordering for bounds and non-throwing C arithmetic for split-quality estimates.
user_visible_surface: Changed on-disk shape and size of existing and new cube GiST indexes; no new SQL objects, GUCs or C API.
author_claims: For 4000 sorted 2-D cubes, insertion drops from about 111 s to about 0.02 s and the index from 33712 to 36 pages.
The reviewer reports patched indexes are never larger than master at 20k rows across eight data shapes, with equal or fewer buffers per query.
v2 fixes the NaN "division by zero" and the large-coordinate overflow errors found in review.
v2 adds regression tests for NaN, infinite, extreme finite and underflow coordinates, for both insertion and create index.
brief.thread_state: Rustam Allakov reviewed v1: index scans agreed with seq scans, but NaN and very large coordinates made inserts and create index fail with an error. Andrey posted v2 with fixes and tests on 2026-11-02; nobody has reviewed v2 yet.
unclear: No benchmark numbers for v2, and no check that the v2 changes keep the v1 split quality.
No numbers for random or unsorted insertion time, only for sorted input and page counts.
The thread does not say whether existing indexes need a reindex after upgrade or whether mixed old and new splits cause any issue.
No numbers for CPU cost of the split itself with many dimensions, up to the cube maximum.
search_queries: GiST unbalanced page split sorted input

refuted.title: Second copy of the double-sorting split, already diverging from box
refuted.failure_scenario: Someone later fixes a split-quality or edge-case bug in gist_box_picksplit(), for example the overflow on large coordinates noted in message #2. Nothing fails or warns if the cube copy is not updated, so the two algorithms drift further apart. Users then see box and cube indexes behave differently on the same data.
refuted.argument: v2-0002 reimplements the box and point algorithm in contrib/cube/cube.c rather than sharing it, and v2 already changes NaN and overflow handling in the cube copy only. Message #2 says the box opclass still raises the overflow error that v2 removes for cube. The proposal does not say whether the generalized N-dimensional split could serve box and point as well, or why two copies are better than one. Copying existing practice lowers the design risk, but it doubles the code that a future GiST fix must find.
refuted.author_must_show: Could the generalized split live in one shared place used by box, point and cube, and if not, why are two diverging copies preferable?

critic.reasoning: Each GiST opclass already keeps its own picksplit, and range types have a separate double-sorting split in rangetypes_gist.c, so the patch follows existing practice. Box and cube already split differently on master, and a missed split fix changes index quality only, not query results.

questions: Does v2 keep the v1 page counts and buffers per query on the eight data shapes from message #2?
How does insertion time and CREATE INDEX time compare with master for random, unsorted input?
What is the CPU cost of one split at high dimensionality, up to the cube maximum of dimensions?
Is there any input that master indexes and v2 still rejects with an ERROR, beyond the cases covered by the new tests?
Can the commit message state that existing cube GiST indexes need no reindex and that old and new splits can coexist in one index?

committability.owner_note: A committer who knows GiST picksplit and the float8 edge cases (NaN, infinity, overflow) in the geometric opclasses would have to own it. None has spoken in the visible thread.
committability.liability: The owner signs for the cube split behaviour on all inputs, including NaN and extreme coordinates, and for any later report of worse index quality on some data shape. The exposure is limited to contrib/cube GiST users.
committability.author_follow_up: The author answered the review in message #3 with v2, fixes for both reported errors and new tests, which suggests he stays for fixes.

priority.reason: The patch touches one file in contrib/cube plus tests and adds no SQL objects, GUCs or C API, and message #1 shows a very large gain for sorted input. Review cost is medium because the float8 edge cases need care and v2 is unreviewed.

provisional_note: The code was not read, so the v2 handling of NaN, infinite and extreme coordinates could not be checked. Split quality of v2 and split CPU cost at many dimensions are also unverified.

precedents_retrieved.title: Index Only Scan support for cube
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a GiST fetch function for the cube extension so that queries on cube columns can use Index Only Scans. It reuses g_cube_decompress() as the fetch function, since both only need to detoast the key.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew it as obsolete after commit d3a4f89 (Allow no-op GiST support functions to be omitted). He said he would work on a broader patch for contrib modules to support GiST Index Only Scans and remove no-op support functions.

precedents_retrieved.title: Cube extension GiST penalty function improvement
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Tom Lane, Greg Stark, Heikki Linnakangas
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes the cube extension's GiST penalty function to follow the RR*-tree choose-subtree rules, preferring entries that need no enlargement and using edge sum (margin) for zero-volume cases. It packs several ranked criteria into one float by reinterpreting its IEEE 754 bit pattern, and later versions fall back to the old penalty when __STDC_IEC_559__ is not defined.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane and Greg Stark objected to the float bit-twiddling because project policy does not allow code to assume IEEE 754, and the author himself later called the technique controversial. Heikki Linnakangas then asked why the patch uses edge sums instead of the volume of the non-zero dimensions, and the thread stalled. Michael Paquier marked the patch returned with feedback, and the author said a planned GiST API and cube patch would make this one unnecessary.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: This thread has basically died, so marking as returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Cube extension kNN support
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds kNN distance operators to the cube extension (<#> taxicab, <-> euclidean, <=> chebyshev) so that ORDER BY ... LIMIT queries can use the index. It also adds a "->" operator to read rows ordered by one coordinate directly from the index, with a minus sign for descending order.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The last review asked for an extension version bump to 1.1 with a cube--1.0--1.1.sql migration script, because the patch changes the extension interface. It also asked to keep the old C name behind cube_distance so an old extension definition works with the new binary. The visible messages show no reply to that review before the entry was returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Since we change the interface of extension we have to change it version and
create a migration script.

precedents_retrieved.title: amcheck verification for GiST
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a GiST verification function to contrib/amcheck that checks parent/child key consistency and that all leaf pages are at the same depth. Later versions hold buffer locks on parent and child pages together and take only an AccessShareLock on the relation.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Geoghegan questioned whether the checks are safe under an AccessShareLock, since Heikki's v6 had used a ShareLock. He doubted that the parent re-find logic copied from gistfinishsplit() applies here and asked how concurrent page deletion could affect it. Andrey Borodin did not answer these questions for about two months, so Michael Paquier returned the entry with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: My main concern now is the heavyweight lock strength needed by the new function.

precedents_retrieved.title: sort leaf pages by ctid for gist indexes built using sorted method
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch sorts index tuples on GiST leaf pages by heap TID when the index is built with the sorted (sortsupport) method. The goal is to keep tuples from the same heap page close together on index pages, so scans avoid reading a heap page twice and prefetch works better.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andrey Borodin measured about 5% slower CREATE INDEX and asked for benchmarks showing a scan benefit, but the author did not respond. Andres Freund returned the entry because that request went unanswered for more than one commitfest and the patch no longer applied.

precedents_retrieved.title: Sort leaf pages by ctid for gist indexes built using sorting method
precedents_retrieved.summary: For GiST indexes built with the sorted (sortsupport) build method, the patch sorts index tuples on leaf pages by heap TID, so that leaf order follows heap order as it does for indexes built by repeated inserts. The goal was to avoid reading the same heap page more than once and to improve prefetching during scans.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The only reply, from Andrey Borodin, supported the idea, measured roughly a 5% slowdown in CREATE INDEX, and asked for benchmarks showing the scan benefit. The entry was withdrawn the next day with no further message shown.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found. [P3] is the same author's 2016 change to the cube penalty function, which is a different proposal; its recorded reason, IEEE 754 bit tricks inside the float penalty, does not apply to a picksplit change. [P17] is about NaN in geo_ops and records no reason. Message #1 links a 2016 discussion where the author first saw unbalanced cube trees, and the thread reports no rejection of a split change from it.

The patch adds no SQL objects, keywords, GUCs, psql features or C API. It changes only how cube GiST pages split, so existing query results stay the same, and old and new indexes are both valid GiST trees that pg_upgrade keeps without a reindex. Message #2 showed that v1 broke pg_dump restore: CREATE INDEX failed on NaN and large coordinates that master accepts. Message #3 says v2 fixes this and adds tests for insertion and CREATE INDEX. Nobody has checked v2 yet. If a v2 review finds any input that master indexes and v2 rejects, the pg_dump round-trip objection applies again.

The patch changes only how cube picksplit distributes entries. The index tuple format, WAL records, catalog, extension SQL objects and C API stay the same. GiST correctness does not depend on the split algorithm, so existing indexes stay valid after pg_upgrade without a reindex, and pages split by the old and new code can coexist in one index. Standbys replay the resulting pages and never run picksplit, so physical replication is not affected, and neither are mixed-version standbys. Message #2 found a dump-and-restore failure on NaN and extreme coordinates, and v2 says it fixes it with tests. That claim concerns the implementation, and nobody has reviewed v2 yet, so it could not be checked from this angle.

The patch changes only the picksplit method of the cube GiST opclass. It adds no SQL objects, privileges, GUCs or monitoring output, so nobody gains new access or new information. A split handles at most one page of entries, so its sorting cost is bounded and does not create a new denial-of-service path. The ERRORs that blocked inserts and restores were reported in message #2 as robustness problems, and v2 says it fixes them. Whether that fix holds needs a check of the code, which this angle does not judge.

Within the maintenance and fit angle, costs fall only on users of contrib/cube with GiST indexes, the design copies existing core practice, and no new GUC, catalog, API or dependency is added. No committer has engaged in the visible thread, which affects committability, not the merits.

No existing feature does this job. Postgres offers no way to swap the picksplit of the cube GiST opclass, and the box opclass covers only two dimensions. The patch reuses the double-sorting split from the box and point opclasses inside an existing contrib module, so it adds no second mechanism and needs no new hook. Precedent P3 changed the penalty function and was returned over IEEE 754 bit-twiddling, which does not apply here.

From the demand angle there is no objection to send. The patch fixes a measured defect in an existing contrib opclass and adds no SQL objects, GUCs or C API. Its cost falls only on contrib/cube GiST users, who also get the benefit. Message #1 shows sorted input making insertion quadratic and the index about 1000 times larger. In message #2 the reviewer found smaller or equal indexes and fewer buffers per query across eight data shapes, including random ones. No field reports are cited, but a defect fix in a shipped opclass does not need the demand evidence a new feature needs. Not checked here: CPU cost of the split at high dimensionality, and whether v2 keeps the v1 split quality.
